QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_43

answer.text: Avoid, disclose, and manage material conflicts; do not recommend schemes based on commissions or pecuniary interests

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 274-278), distributors should avoid practices involving professional conflicts or anything that jeopardises investor interests, must not market/sell products where they have potential conflicts, should avoid soft-dollar arrangements and pass-backs, must ensure material conflicts are disclosed before investment decisions, keep investor interest and suitability paramount, and must not recommend schemes solely because of higher commissions. The Trap: Hiding conflicts, chasing the highest-commission product, or treating conflicts as inevitable all violate the workbook's standard of professional conduct. Note: Disclose first, recommend second — investors must be able to factor any conflict into their own decision before they commit capital.
